title.value: Impact of a vaccine passport on first-dose COVID-19 vaccine coverage by age and area-level social determinants in the Canadian provinces of Québec and Ontario: an interrupted time series analysis
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the study: assessing the impact of vaccine passport policies on first-dose COVID-19 vaccine coverage across different demographics and areas in Québec and Ontario.
title.quote: Impact of a vaccine passport on first-dose COVID-19 vaccine coverage by age and area-level social determinants in the Canadian provinces of Québec and Ontario: an interrupted time series analysis

extractions.description: The paper evaluates the impact of vaccine passport policies on first-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage in Canadian provinces Québec and Ontario. It analyzes the effects by age, area-level income, and proportion racialized using an interrupted time-series methodology.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme revolves around the impact of vaccine passports on COVID-19 vaccine uptake, which is more directly related to public health policy rather than climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Background: In Canada, all provinces implemented vaccine passports in 2021 to increase vaccine uptake and reduce transmission in non-essential indoor spaces.

primary_category.justification: The study focuses primarily on public health and vaccine policy impacts, which do not align with any specified climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: We evaluate the impact of vaccine passport policies on first-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage by age, area-level income and proportion racialized.

secondary_categories.justification: The entire paper is focused on public health intervention analysis with no emphasis on climate or ecological themes.
secondary_categories.quote: Conclusions: In the context of high baseline vaccine coverage across two provinces, the announcement of vaccine passports led to a small impact on first-dose coverage, with little impact on reducing economic and racial inequities in vaccine coverage.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no appropriate sub-category within the climate or ecological sustainable development contexts that this paper could fit into.
primary_sub_category.quote: Keywords: Vaccination; vaccine mandates; vaccine passports; COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2; social determinants of health; Canada; interrupted time-series.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The discussion of social determinants of health in the context of vaccine uptake does not relate directly to environmental or climate-focused sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We investigated heterogeneity in the impact of vaccine passports by age and by area-level SDOH, which have been associated with higher COVID-19 infection burden.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper’s core focus is on vaccine policy impacts in public health rather than on developing solutions or models relevant to climate or ecological sustainability.
new_primary_category.quote: Background: In Canada, all provinces implemented vaccine passports in 2021 to increase vaccine uptake and reduce transmission in non-essential indoor spaces.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Evaluating the impact of vaccine policy does not warrant the creation of a new sub-category within the climate or ecological contexts.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In both provinces, pre-announcement first-dose vaccination coverage was 82% (≥12 years).
